steps.action: An over-long filename is refused with actionable copy, and a corrected name uploads exactly once
steps.actual: A 318-character filename was refused with copy naming the filename problem, and nothing was stored. Renaming to "Docs V-C49 corrected name.pdf" stored it once. Checking the destination list before retrying, as the article says, is what shows whether the first attempt landed.

steps.action: A damaged Word file reaches the article's failure message and its original still downloads
steps.actual: Reviewer check did not complete: Error: the damaged file did not reach the documented failure (pending seen: false)

steps.action: The preference pane shows the In-app and Email choices and states the rule the article gives
steps.actual: The staff pane lists each event group with its In-app and Email switches and a Briefing section, and states "Email off keeps the bell items coming. In-app off turns the group off entirely, email included." That is the app's own wording for the article's sentence that turning In-app off also stops that group's new email. No preference was changed.

steps.action: The Portal reader finds Request updates under Notification settings
steps.actual: As the Business User, Notification settings in the Portal offered "Request updates", which is the control the article tells this reader to check.

fixturePreparation: Uploaded fictional files to C-56 through the app's own Upload control: a small valid PDF under an over-long name, the same PDF under a corrected name, and a deliberately damaged archive named .docx.
Approval requests were created through the API as the Administrator so that the decision itself could be followed in the browser as the named approver.
limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.
The Signing connector is not configured and the AI connector is disabled in this lab. Those steps record an unconfigured state only and do not satisfy C42/C43, which stay blocked on #742.
Email delivery itself was not re-tested here; only the preference surfaces the article tells the reader to check.
